name: Tessier Number 4 Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a cleft extending from the lip through the maxillary region following the Tessier number 4 anatomical line
Involvement of the lower eyelid and infraorbital rim with soft tissue and bony defects
Associated nasal ala and lateral nasal wall deformities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cleft along Tessier number 4 anatomical line with orbital involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging studies to assess bony involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lateral orofacial cleft extending from lip to infraorbital region
Maxillary bone defect along cleft line
searchTerms: bone gap in upper jaw near cleft
jaw bone defect at cleft site

common.symptomName: Soft tissue deficiency in midface region
searchTerms: lack of soft tissue in midface

common.symptomName: Dental anomalies including missing or malformed teeth
searchTerms: teeth that are malformed or absent

common.symptomName: Epiphora due to lacrimal duct involvement
searchTerms: excessive tearing from blocked tear duct
watery eyes due to lacrimal issues

occasional.symptomName: Chronic sinusitis secondary to anatomical defects
searchTerms: repeated sinusitis due to facial defects
sinus problems caused by structural issues

occasional.symptomName: Hearing impairment due to middle ear anomalies
searchTerms: hearing loss from middle ear problems
ear canal or bone anomalies causing deafness
impaired hearing due to ear malformation

rare.symptomName: Cleft palate involvement beyond primary cleft line

imaging: CT scan showing bony defects along the maxilla and infraorbital rim
MRI to evaluate soft tissue and orbital involvement
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic cleft morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Cleft line more medial involving the nasolacrimal duct and medial canthus
Different orbital and nasal deformity pattern
Presence of ear anomalies and vertebral defects
Unilateral facial microsomia rather than midfacial cleft

redFlags: Airway obstruction due to midface deformity
Associated intracranial anomalies or neurological deficits
references: Tessier P. Anatomical classification of facial clefts. J Maxillofac Surg. 1976.
